## Overview

::: {.callout-important}
## Research Plan Due Friday 27 February, 12 noon
Use this self-assessment **before you submit**. Work through each section to check your Research Plan covers everything it needs to. This is not graded — it's a tool to help you submit your best work.
:::

Your Research Plan (1,000–1,200 words) is structured like a Method section. It should include: a hypothesis, design, participants, materials, procedure, and statistical test — all with justification.

---

## Section 1: Hypothesis

A clear, testable hypothesis is the foundation of your Research Plan.

**1. Does your hypothesis name the independent variable?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — the IV is clearly stated</option><option value=''>No — I need to add this</option><option value=''>I'm not sure what the IV is</option></select>

**2. Does your hypothesis name the dependent variable?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — the DV is clearly stated</option><option value=''>No — I need to add this</option><option value=''>I'm not sure what the DV is</option></select>

**3. Is your hypothesis directional (one-tailed) or non-directional (two-tailed)?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>One-tailed — I predict a specific direction</option><option value=''>Two-tailed — I predict a difference but not the direction</option><option value='answer'>I have stated which it is and explained why</option></select>

**4. Is your hypothesis testable with the statistical test you've chosen?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — my hypothesis maps onto my test</option><option value=''>I think so but I'm not certain</option><option value=''>No — I need to revise</option></select>

### Self-Check

::: {.webex-check .webex-box}

**A good hypothesis should:**

Name both the IV and DV: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

Include the word "significant": <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

State a predicted direction (if one-tailed): <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

Be based on previous research or theory: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

Include statistical values: <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>
:::

---

## Section 2: Design

Your design section should tell the reader exactly how the study is structured.

**1. Have you stated the type of design?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — between-subjects or within-subjects is clearly stated</option><option value=''>I've mentioned the design but not the type</option><option value=''>I haven't included this yet</option></select>

**2. Have you justified your design choice?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — I've explained WHY this design was chosen</option><option value=''>I've stated the design but not explained why</option><option value=''>I haven't thought about justification</option></select>

**3. Have you identified the IV with its levels?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — IV named with both/all levels specified</option><option value=''>I've named the IV but not the levels</option><option value=''>I need to add this</option></select>

**4. Have you identified the DV and how it's measured?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — DV named with measurement method</option><option value=''>I've named the DV but not how it's measured</option><option value=''>I need to add this</option></select>

### Common Design Mistakes

**Which of these is a problem?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Stating that a between-subjects design avoids order effects</option><option value='answer'>Stating the design type without explaining why it was chosen</option><option value=''>Mentioning potential confounding variables</option><option value=''>Including both IV and DV</option></select>

**"A between-subjects design was used" is:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>A complete design section</option><option value='answer'>Missing justification, IV, DV, and levels</option><option value=''>Too detailed</option><option value=''>Only missing the DV</option></select>

True or False: You should explain why your design is appropriate, not just name it. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

True or False: A within-subjects design always requires counterbalancing. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

---

## Section 3: Participants

Your participants section tells the reader who would take part and how they'd be recruited.

**1. Have you stated the total number of participants?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — with numbers per condition if between-subjects</option><option value=''>I've given a total but not per condition</option><option value=''>I haven't specified a number</option></select>

**2. Have you described the recruitment method?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — e.g., opportunity sampling from the student population</option><option value=''>I've mentioned sampling but not the method</option><option value=''>I haven't included this</option></select>

**3. Have you included demographic information?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — age range, mean age, gender breakdown</option><option value=''>I've included some demographics</option><option value=''>I haven't included demographics</option></select>

**4. Have you mentioned inclusion/exclusion criteria?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — e.g., native English speakers, aged 18+</option><option value=''>I've thought about it but not written it</option><option value=''>I haven't considered this</option></select>

### Self-Check

**A Participants subsection should be written in:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Present tense</option><option value='answer'>Past tense (or future tense for a plan)</option><option value=''>First person</option><option value=''>Bullet points</option></select>

**Which is better?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>20 people took part</option><option value='answer'>Twenty participants (12 female, 8 male; M_age = 20.5, SD = 1.8) were recruited via opportunity sampling from the student population at Goldsmiths, University of London</option><option value=''>We tested some students from our class</option></select>

True or False: You should justify your sample size if possible. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

True or False: "Some people" is an acceptable description of participants. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

---

## Section 4: Materials

Your materials section describes everything you need to run the study.

**1. Have you described your stimuli (e.g., word lists, images, questionnaires)?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — with examples of specific items</option><option value=''>I've mentioned materials but without examples</option><option value=''>I haven't described materials yet</option></select>

**2. Have you explained how materials were created or selected?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — I've explained the source or construction method</option><option value=''>I've listed materials but not their origin</option><option value=''>I haven't included this</option></select>

**3. Have you mentioned any key properties of your materials?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — e.g., number of items, matching for word frequency/length</option><option value=''>Some properties are mentioned</option><option value=''>I haven't included properties</option></select>

### Self-Check

**Which materials description is stronger?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>We used a word list</option><option value=''>A list of words was prepared for the experiment</option><option value='answer'>Two word lists were constructed, each containing 15 words. The concrete list contained words referring to physical objects (e.g., hammer, bicycle). Lists were matched for word frequency using the MRC Psycholinguistic Database.</option></select>

True or False: You should give examples of your stimuli (e.g., sample words from a list). <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

True or False: "We used some materials" is sufficient for this section. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

---

## Section 5: Procedure

Your procedure is a chronological account of what participants would experience.

**1. Is your procedure written in chronological order?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — step by step from start to finish</option><option value=''>Mostly, but some steps are out of order</option><option value=''>I need to reorganise</option></select>

**2. Have you included timing for each phase?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — e.g., '2 minutes to study', '1 minute distractor task'</option><option value=''>Some timings are mentioned</option><option value=''>I haven't included timings</option></select>

**3. Have you mentioned informed consent?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — participants provide consent before the study begins</option><option value=''>I've implied it but not stated it</option><option value=''>I haven't mentioned consent</option></select>

**4. Have you mentioned debriefing?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — participants are debriefed at the end</option><option value=''>I've implied it</option><option value=''>I haven't mentioned debriefing</option></select>

**5. Is there enough detail for someone to replicate your study?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — another researcher could follow my procedure</option><option value=''>Mostly, but some details are vague</option><option value=''>Probably not — I need more detail</option></select>

### Common Procedure Mistakes

**Which of these is a problem in a Procedure section?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Including the timing of each phase</option><option value='answer'>Including the results of the study</option><option value=''>Mentioning the distractor task</option><option value=''>Describing how consent was obtained</option></select>

**"Participants did the experiment and then we collected the data" is:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>Adequate</option><option value='answer'>Far too vague — needs step-by-step detail</option><option value=''>Appropriate for a Research Plan</option><option value=''>Only missing one detail</option></select>

True or False: The Procedure should mention ethical safeguards (consent and debrief). <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

True or False: You should include your actual results in the Procedure section. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

---

## Section 6: Statistical Test

Your Research Plan should name and justify the statistical test you plan to use.

**1. Have you named the specific statistical test?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — e.g., independent-samples t-test or paired-samples t-test</option><option value=''>I've said 't-test' but not which type</option><option value=''>I haven't named a test</option></select>

**2. Have you justified why this test is appropriate?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — I've linked it to my design, IV levels, and DV measurement</option><option value=''>I've named the test but not justified it</option><option value=''>I haven't thought about justification</option></select>

**3. Does your test match your design?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — between-subjects → independent t-test, within-subjects → paired t-test</option><option value=''>I think so</option><option value=''>I'm not sure which test matches which design</option></select>

### Self-Check

**An independent-samples t-test is used when:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>The same participants are in both conditions</option><option value='answer'>Different participants are in each condition</option><option value=''>There are more than two conditions</option><option value=''>The data is categorical</option></select>

**A paired-samples t-test is used when:**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>The same participants are in both conditions</option><option value=''>Different participants are in each condition</option><option value=''>You want to compare three groups</option><option value=''>The DV is nominal</option></select>

True or False: You should explain why your chosen test is appropriate for your design. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

True or False: A t-test can compare more than two groups. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value=''>TRUE</option><option value='answer'>FALSE</option></select>

---

## Section 7: Writing Quality

Finally, check the quality of your writing.

**1. Is your Research Plan written in past tense (or planned future tense)?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — consistent tense throughout</option><option value=''>Mostly, but some present tense slips in</option><option value=''>I'm not sure about tense</option></select>

**2. Is it written in third person?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — 'Participants were asked...' not 'I asked...'</option><option value=''>Mostly, but I've used 'I' or 'we' in places</option><option value=''>I've written in first person throughout</option></select>

**3. Is it within the word count (1,000–1,200 words)?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — I've checked</option><option value=''>I'm close but haven't checked exactly</option><option value=''>I'm over or under</option></select>

**4. Have you proofread for spelling and grammar?**

<select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>Yes — I've read through it carefully</option><option value=''>I've done a quick check</option><option value=''>Not yet</option></select>

### Final Check

True or False: "I will ask participants to..." should be "Participants will be asked to..." <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

True or False: Statistical symbols like *t*, *p*, and *M* should be italicised. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

True or False: You should include a reference list if you cite any sources. <select class='webex-select'><option value='blank'></option><option value='answer'>TRUE</option><option value=''>FALSE</option></select>

---

## Final Checklist

::: {.callout-important}
## Before You Submit — Check Every Box

- [ ] **Hypothesis**: Specific, testable, names IV and DV, states direction
- [ ] **Design**: Type stated and justified, IV with levels, DV with measurement
- [ ] **Participants**: Number, recruitment method, demographics, criteria
- [ ] **Materials**: Described with examples, source/construction explained
- [ ] **Procedure**: Chronological, timed, detailed enough to replicate
- [ ] **Ethics**: Informed consent and debriefing mentioned
- [ ] **Statistical test**: Named and justified, matches design
- [ ] **Writing**: Past/future tense, third person, academic tone
- [ ] **Word count**: 1,000–1,200 words
- [ ] **Proofread**: Spelling, grammar, APA conventions

**Submit via Learn by Friday 27 February, 12 noon.**
:::

---

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

::: {.callout-warning}
## Don't Do These

1. **No justification** — "A between-subjects design was used" without explaining why
2. **Too vague** — "Some people did a test" instead of precise details
3. **Wrong tense** — "Participants will sit down and I give them the words"
4. **Including results** — the Method describes what you *plan to do*, not what you *found*
5. **Missing ethics** — forgetting to mention consent and debriefing
6. **No examples** — "A word list was used" without saying what kind of words
7. **Wrong test** — choosing an independent t-test for a within-subjects design
8. **First person** — "I decided to use..." instead of "An X design was employed because..."
:::
